correctness.rationale: The polar is the bounded unit-Lipschitz polytope of KG(5,2). Its vertices are precisely integral potentials with connected unit-tight edges. The graph has diameter two, so levels are 0,1,2. A complete finite cross-intersecting-family lemma bounds the extreme level classes, yielding maximum squared centered norm 28/5 exactly for the 30 signed graph-edge configurations. Every such configuration has connected tight graph, so these are actual polar vertices and exactly the tangent facets. Central symmetry makes the origin-centered inradius globally optimal; the explicit 15-normal Gram matrix has positive eigenvalues 1 (multiplicity 4) and 16 (multiplicity 5) on the zero-sum hyperplane, forcing the center to be unique. The standalone standard-library enumerator exhaustively checks 1410 polar vertices, 30 maximizers and the rank-nine Gram matrix using exact arithmetic.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical vertex-transitive cubic strongly regular graph, and its nine-dimensional symmetric edge polytope is a natural, uniquely specified object. The result establishes the exact radius, entire contact-facet orbit and uniqueness of all insphere centers, as opposed to an arbitrary computational slice or mere facet recount. The cross-intersection inequality and Gram rank exhibit two independent structural mechanisms. The exact contact orbit is a meaningful benchmark for comparing polytope geometry to graph-spread extremizers.
